evals.name: audience-table-and-diátaxis
evals.prompt: You maintain a Python library called `slugify-utils` v0.3.2. It exposes three public functions: `slugify(text, lang='en')`, `validate_slug(s)`, and `unslugify(slug)`. It supports English, Russian, and Czech transliteration. About 50 internal teams import it. Generate the documentation portfolio for this library. Save every file to the CURRENT directory. Do not ask clarifying questions — make reasonable assumptions. Print the list of files you wrote at the end.
evals.expected_output: README with Target Audiences table, doc plan with Diátaxis types and P0/P1/P2 priorities, and at least one Tutorial file with Doc-Type label + Before You Begin + What You Will Learn sections.
expectations: A '## Target Audiences' section is present in README.md OR in a separate AUDIENCES.md file, containing a table with AT LEAST 2 distinct named personas — each row must have a non-empty Role AND a non-empty 'First Doc to Read' column. Generic entries like 'Developer' without a role do NOT satisfy this; named personas like 'Library Consumer / Backend engineer' DO.

A documentation plan section or file is present that contains BOTH: (a) a 'Diátaxis Type' or equivalent column with values from Tutorial/How-To/Reference/Explanation, AND (b) a priority column using P0/P1/P2 notation. A plan with numbered bullets or a flat list but no priority tier notation does NOT satisfy this.

At least one generated file contains the comment '<!-- Doc-Type: Tutorial -->' OR '<!-- Doc-Type: How-To -->' OR '<!-- Doc-Type: Reference -->' OR '<!-- Doc-Type: Explanation -->' as a line in the file. Files without any Doc-Type comment do NOT satisfy this — the label must literally appear in the output.

evals.name: adr-heading-and-quality-score
evals.prompt: You are documenting an existing internal e-commerce system named `orderflow`. It has 4 services: `api-gateway` (Go), `order-service` (Python/FastAPI), `payment-service` (Python/FastAPI, owns Stripe integration), and `notification-service` (Node.js). They communicate via REST and a Kafka topic `order.events`. The team just decided to migrate from REST to gRPC for inter-service calls. Generate the architecture documentation set for this system, including the migration decision. Save every file to the CURRENT directory. Do not ask clarifying questions. Print the list of files at the end.
evals.expected_output: ADR with ## Status as a heading (not a table row), 3+ architecture files, and a Documentation Quality Score section with a numeric total/100.
expectations: At least one ADR file contains '## Status' as a markdown heading (a line starting with exactly '## Status', case-insensitive). A table row like '| Status | Accepted |' does NOT satisfy this — the heading form is required. This tests that the skill's ADR template format is followed rather than the MADR table convention baseline models default to.

A '## Documentation Quality Score' section OR a 'Documentation Quality Score' table appears somewhere in the output — either in README.md or a dedicated QUALITY.md — containing a numeric score expressed as X/100. A qualitative rating like 'Good' without a number does NOT satisfy this.

A '## Known Gaps' section OR a GAPS.md file appears in the output. It must contain either: (a) at least one gap row in a table, OR (b) the literal text 'No known gaps' followed by a date. Complete absence of any known gaps section does NOT satisfy this.

evals.name: tutorial-required-sections
evals.prompt: Your team is handing off a 2-year-old internal tool called `metrics-dashboard` to a different department. Stack: Python/Flask backend, React frontend, PostgreSQL, deployed on Kubernetes via Helm. About 200 daily users across product, ops, and finance teams. The receiving team has 3 mid-level engineers and 1 ops person; they have never seen this codebase. Produce the handoff documentation package. Save every file to the CURRENT directory. Do not ask clarifying questions. Print the list of files at the end.
evals.expected_output: A tutorial or getting-started doc with Before You Begin + What You Will Learn sections, a doc plan with P0/P1/P2 tiers, and a Documentation Quality Score section.
expectations: At least one documentation file contains BOTH a '## Before You Begin' section (with a prerequisite list or checklist) AND a '## What You Will Learn' section (with bulleted learning outcomes). Both sections must appear in the same file. A file with only one of the two does NOT satisfy this — both are required for a Tutorial per the skill's Phase 3 specification.

A documentation plan, handoff plan, or index file contains explicit P0/P1/P2 priority markers — the literal strings 'P0', 'P1', or 'P2' must appear as priority labels in a table or section heading. Timing-based language like 'Read First: Yes' or 'Week 1' does NOT satisfy this — the P0/P1/P2 scheme is required.

At least one documentation file contains the comment '<!-- Doc-Type: Tutorial -->' as a line in the file AND that same file has a '## Before You Begin' section. The Doc-Type label and the required tutorial section must co-occur in the same file — a label without the section, or a section without the label, does NOT satisfy this.
